reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet, ranking tenth among Texas data centers with disclosed power figures and holding 4 percent of the state's total mapped capacity.

The facility holds certifications for regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and government, including PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II. This positions it to serve compliance-sensitive workloads but not the scale at which frontier AI training now operates. Hyperscaler campuses driving current model development commonly exceed 100 MW of IT load. At 19 MW, this facility sits below the threshold where compute density and power envelope enable large-scale training clusters.

Austin has 133 mapped data center facilities in total but only four with published megawatt figures. CyrusOne's transparency on capacity places it in the upper tier of disclosed operators statewide. However, published megawatts across Texas remain modest relative to the power demands now required for frontier model training. The state's disclosed capacity of 468 MW reflects what operators choose to report, not total deployed infrastructure, leaving the true picture of available AI-ready buildings and power in the region incomplete.
